es.summary: Trastorno respiratorio caracterizado por interrupciones repetidas de la respiración durante el sueño, que provocan hipoxemia y sueño fragmentado.
key_points: Obstrucción de la vía aérea superior es la causa principal de la apnea obstructiva.
El índice de apnea‑hipopnea (IAH) >5 eventos/hora confirma el diagnóstico.
CPAP es el tratamiento de primera línea para la mayoría de los adultos.
Complicaciones incluyen hipertensión, enfermedad cardiovascular y somnolencia diurna.
La pérdida de peso y la higiene del sueño mejoran significativamente los síntomas.

pathophysiology: Colapso de la vía aérea superior durante la fase de sueño REM.
Interrupción del flujo de aire produce hipoxemia y aumento de CO₂.
Despertar breve (arousal) restaura la respiración pero fragmenta el sueño.
Repetidos ciclos generan estrés simpático y elevación de la presión arterial.
risk_factors: Historia familiar de apnea del sueño.
Vías aéreas estrechas: amígdalas/adenóides agrandadas en niños.
signs_symptoms: Pausas respiratorias observadas por el acompañante.
Somnolencia diurna, fatiga y dificultad de concentración.
Cefalea matutina y boca seca al despertar.
diagnostics: Polisomnografía completa: IAH >5 eventos/hora confirma apnea.
Escala de Epworth de somnolencia diurna: puntuación >10 indica somnolencia excesiva.
treatment: Cambios de estilo de vida: pérdida de peso, evitar alcohol y sedantes.
CPAP (presión positiva continua en las vías respiratorias).
Dispositivo de avance mandibular para casos leves‑moderados.
Cirugía de vía aérea (uvulopalatofaringoplastia) cuando otras medidas fallan.
complications: Accidentes de tránsito y laborales por somnolencia.
nursing_care: Evaluar patrón respiratorio y saturación O₂ durante la noche.
Enseñar uso correcto y mantenimiento del CPAP.
Posicionar al paciente en decúbito lateral si no usa CPAP.
Registrar episodios de apnea y somnolencia diurna.
Monitorear presión arterial y glucemia según riesgo cardiovascular.
patient_teaching: Importancia de la adherencia al CPAP (≥4 h/noche).
Higiene del sueño: horarios regulares, ambiente oscuro y sin dispositivos electrónicos.
Dieta balanceada y ejercicio para reducir peso.
Evitar alcohol y sedantes antes de acostarse.

outcomes: Patrón respiratorio eficaz: mantener saturación O₂ ≥92 % durante el sueño.
Reducción de episodios de apnea a <5 eventos/hora en la polisomnografía de seguimiento.

interventions.action: Monitorear saturación de oxígeno nocturna con pulsioxímetro.
interventions.rationale: Detecta hipoxemia y permite evaluar la efectividad del CPAP.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente la colocación y ajuste del CPAP.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la adherencia y reduce los episodios de apnea.

interventions.action: Posicionar al paciente en decúbito lateral si no usa CPAP.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la colapsabilidad de la vía aérea superior.

interventions.action: Registrar número de despertares y episodios de apnea cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Proporciona datos objetivos para el equipo de salud.

interventions.action: Evaluar presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca cada 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifica complicaciones cardiovasculares asociadas.

outcomes: Nivel de energía: reportar ≥7/10 en escala de energía al final del día.
Somnolencia diurna: reducir episodios de sueño involuntario a <1 por día.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y somnolencia usando la escala de Epworth.
interventions.rationale: Establece línea base y permite medir progreso.

interventions.action: Planificar descansos cortos de 10‑15 min cada 2 h de actividad.
interventions.rationale: Previene agotamiento y mejora la concentración.

interventions.action: Reforzar educación sobre higiene del sueño y uso del CPAP.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la calidad del sueño y reduce la fatiga diurna.

interventions.action: Coordinar con nutricionista para plan de pérdida de peso.
interventions.rationale: Reducción de peso disminuye la gravedad de la apnea.

interventions.action: Fomentar actividad física moderada (30 min/día).
interventions.rationale: Aumenta energía y contribuye al control del peso.

en.summary: Respiratory disorder characterized by repeated interruptions of breathing during sleep, causing hypoxemia and fragmented sleep.
key_points: Upper airway obstruction is the primary cause of obstructive sleep apnea.
An apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) >5 events/hour confirms the diagnosis.
CPAP is first-line treatment for most adults.
Complications include hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and daytime sleepiness.
Weight loss and sleep hygiene significantly improve symptoms.

pathophysiology: Upper airway collapse during REM sleep.
Airflow interruption produces hypoxemia and increased CO₂.
Brief arousals restore breathing but fragment sleep.
Repeated cycles generate sympathetic stress and elevated blood pressure.
risk_factors: Narrow airways: enlarged tonsils/adenoids in children.
signs_symptoms: Observed breathing pauses by a partner.
Daytime sleepiness, fatigue, and concentration difficulty.
Morning headache and dry mouth upon awakening.
diagnostics: Full polysomnography: AHI >5 events/hour confirms apnea.
Epworth Sleepiness Scale: score >10 indicates excessive sleepiness.
treatment: Lifestyle changes: weight loss, avoid alcohol and sedatives.
Mandibular advancement device for mild‑moderate cases.
Airway surgery (uvulopalatopharyngoplasty) when other measures fail.
complications: Road and workplace accidents due to sleepiness.
nursing_care: Assess respiratory pattern and O₂ saturation during the night.
Teach proper use and maintenance of CPAP.
Position patient on lateral decubitus if not using CPAP.
Document apnea episodes and daytime sleepiness.
Monitor blood pressure and glucose per cardiovascular risk.
patient_teaching: Sleep hygiene: regular schedule, dark environment, no electronic devices.
Balanced diet and exercise to reduce weight.
Avoid alcohol and sedatives before bedtime.

outcomes: Effective respiratory pattern: maintain O₂ saturation ≥92 % during sleep.
Reduction of apnea episodes to <5 events/hour on follow-up polysomnography.

interventions.action: Monitor nocturnal oxygen saturation with pulse oximeter.
interventions.rationale: Detects hypoxemia and allows evaluation of CPAP effectiveness.

interventions.action: Teach patient placement and adjustment of CPAP.
interventions.rationale: Improves adherence and reduces apnea episodes.

interventions.action: Position patient on lateral decubitus if not using CPAP.
interventions.rationale: Reduces upper airway collapsibility.

interventions.action: Record number of awakenings and apnea episodes each shift.
interventions.rationale: Provides objective data for the health team.

interventions.action: Assess blood pressure and heart rate every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifies associated cardiovascular complications.

outcomes: Energy level: report ≥7/10 on energy scale at end of day.
Daytime sleepiness: reduce involuntary sleep episodes to <1 per day.

interventions.action: Assess energy level and sleepiness using the Epworth Scale.
interventions.rationale: Establishes baseline and allows measurement of progress.

interventions.action: Plan short 10‑15 min breaks every 2 h of activity.
interventions.rationale: Prevents exhaustion and improves concentration.

interventions.action: Reinforce education on sleep hygiene and CPAP use.
interventions.rationale: Improves sleep quality and reduces daytime fatigue.

interventions.action: Coordinate with nutritionist for weight loss plan.
interventions.rationale: Weight reduction decreases apnea severity.

interventions.action: Encourage moderate physical activity (30 min/day).
interventions.rationale: Increases energy and contributes to weight control.

key_points.0.quote: It causes your airway to collapse or become blocked during sleep.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: You are more at risk for sleep apnea if you are overweight, male, or have a family history or small airways.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: You are more at risk for sleep apnea if you are overweight, male, or have a family history or small airways.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Children with enlarged tonsils or adenoids may also get it.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: People with sleep apnea often snore loudly.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Sleep apnea is a common disorder that causes your breathing to stop or get very shallow.

sections.treatment.1.quote: CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure) (National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute) Also in Spanish

sections.complications.0.quote: The risk for developing certain disorders, such as hypertension, coronary artery disease, diabetes mellitus, cancer, depression, and anxiety, is higher for those who experience chronic insomnia.

sections.complications.3.quote: People with sleep apnea are at higher risk for car crashes, work-related accidents, and other medical problems.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: A sleep study, or polysomnography , involves results of assorted physiologic monitors, including EEG, electrocardiogram (ECG), electrooculogram (EOG), electromyogram (EMG), and oxygen saturation (SaO 2 ).

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: Recommendations are to limit alcohol to one or two drinks around the evening meal, then to avoid alcohol for three or four hours prior to bedtime (Krans, 2019; Spadola et al. 2019).
